evals.name: choose-shop-strategies-and-entropy
evals.prompt: On Screenplay 4.151.0, our shop has CustomerId (cus_ plus ULID), OrderId (TypeID) and InviteCode (NanoID). Show their concept generation declarations and a generated CustomerId command property. A shorter InviteCode proposal uses 16 hexadecimal symbols; compute its random bits versus the default NanoID. Does the customer prefix add entropy or guarantee ordering? We also have ApiKey from .NET Bytes(32) with NotAudited and an Arc context-aware OrderId. Which parts can Screenplay execute today? Reply only; no tools or edits.
evals.expected_output: CustomerId is String with generate ulid prefix "cus_"; OrderId uses generate typeid "order"; InviteCode uses generate nanoid. The command property is customerId CustomerId generated identifier, with no per-property strategy. Default NanoID has 126 bits; 16 positions in a 16-symbol alphabet have 64 bits, meeting the identifier floor. Prefixes add none; time order is not monotonic within a millisecond. Preserve ApiKey secret but do not generate it; received-time/tenant context and secret execution remain Screenplay#616 phases 3/4. The ordinary TypeID strategy is not equivalent to Arc's context contract. Separate source, executable and target gates.
assertions: Places ULID/cus_, TypeID/order and NanoID strategies on String concepts and generated identifier on the command property.
Computes 64 random bits for the custom InviteCode and 126 for default NanoID, adds no prefix entropy and rejects strict within-millisecond ordering.
Preserves ApiKey secret classification without claiming executable secret generation, and distinguishes TypeID shape from Arc receipt-time/tenant context.
Separates authoring, binding/reference execution and target support; does not call entropy evidence an executable or render verdict.

evals.name: refuse-gapless-invoice-generation
evals.prompt: Our shop's Screenplay 4.151.0 billing model needs legally gapless invoice numbers shared across concurrent commands. Can generate sequence, random numbers with retries, generate pattern with a date, or generate rule reading the previous invoice solve it today? We also receive a client-minted CustomerId and a webhook idempotency key. Reply only with what to model or leave open, without inventing allocator APIs.
evals.expected_output: None is a released gapless allocator. generate sequence is reserved (PLAY0682); pattern/random/rule parse but refuse executable binding (PLAY0268), and read-then-write plus randomness cannot enforce gapless concurrent allocation. Keep the allocator requirement as an explicit capability gap/owning implementation question (Screenplay#619). CustomerId remains an input; idempotency needs a persisted/deterministic request mapping with independent uniqueness, not new randomness or a future derive promise.
assertions: Refuses randomness, retries and read-then-write as a gapless concurrent invoice allocator.
Names sequence as reserved and pattern/random/rule as non-executable, not shipped solutions.
Preserves the business requirement as an explicit capability gap without inventing a sequence or derive API.
Keeps client-minted CustomerId as input and treats idempotency/uniqueness independently of generation.

evals.name: generation-is-not-protection
evals.prompt: RegisterCustomer on Screenplay 4.151.0 has a cus_-prefixed ULID generated identifier. A teammate wants to use it as the shop ApiKey, remove authorization, and add a generated-concept matches rule because the generation summary reports high entropy. Is that admitted and safe? The MCP executable.status is notAssessed due to another declaration's binding error. Reply only.
evals.expected_output: A time-visible CustomerId is neither a credential nor authorization. Keep the policy and ApiKey secret contract; secret generation and generated-concept validation/rule consistency are not admitted. High entropy does not prove security or rule consistency. notAssessed is unknown due to unrelated binding failure, not admitted; inspect diagnostics and reassess after a scoped repair. Do not invent derived regex/checksum/rule-proof repairs.
assertions: Rejects CustomerId as ApiKey and retains independent authorization and secret classification.
States generated secrets and generated-concept validation/rule consistency are unadmitted, never deletes classification/rules to obtain admission.
Treats notAssessed as unknown rather than admitted and distinguishes entropy from whole-model binding.
Does not promise derived regex, checksum or rule-proof repairs as released capabilities.
